unit: one original unique-address source-row pair; not a confirmed facility identity

method.name: Haversine
method.description: Spherical shortest surface distance in meters. Coordinates interpreted as decimal longitude and latitude; no route, elevation or ellipsoid correction.

validity: Both coordinate pairs must be finite numbers within longitude [-180,180] and latitude [-90,90]. Null or invalid coordinates yield null distance, not zero. Preserve all 75 pairs. A coordinate failing the existing Taipei coarse check remains calculable if globally valid, but carries a quality flag.
ranking: Sort calculated distances descending using unrounded meters, then comparison ID ascending for ties. Unavailable distances last with null rank. Rank is ordinal and does not assert that tied values differ.
summary: Median is the middle value for odd n, mean of two middle values for even n; use only calculated pairs. Empty subsets have null min/median/max, never zero.
display: Store unrounded numeric meters. Display below 0.1 m as <0.1 m; otherwise one decimal meter. Never rank or bucket rounded display text. The displayed decimals do not establish coordinate accuracy.
limits: Same address does not establish the same physical bin. Distances do not confirm relocation, removal or installation.
Coordinate changes can reflect precision, correction, geocoding or data-entry differences; causes require separate evidence.
Spherical distance is an approximation, not walking distance or surveyed movement. No datum transformation or field verification is performed.
The 2024 archive capture is Taipei 2024-10-19 (UTC 2024-10-18), not an original survey/update date. The 2026 source update is 2026-09-30; download 2026-10-15.
Both snapshots have unverified physical citywide completeness. Preserve source IDs, physical start lines, raw coordinates, dates, and original 75-pair membership.
